dossier.name: Todd Boehly
dossier.role: Co-founder, chairman and CEO of Eldridge Industries, and chairman of Eldridge. He was formerly chairman and co-owner of Chelsea FC, which ended in September 2026.
dossier.thesis: Eldridge is a holding company that uses permanent capital from its two insurance businesses, Security Benefit and Everly Life, to make long-term investments in insurance, asset management, technology, real estate, sports and media. Its sports and media strategy centres on companies that own premium intellectual property.
dossier.stages: Not an early-stage VC. It makes strategic, growth and control investments, and sometimes leads a round in a later-stage company (for example Overtime). It also takes ownership stakes in operating companies (for example Sudolabs).
looks_for: Companies with premium intellectual property (sports and entertainment)
Platforms that can scale, such as enterprise AI deployed at scale
Businesses Eldridge can support across its wider portfolio

brief.headline: Eldridge backs scalable platforms built around premium fan IP, and your app turns each fanbase's ticket into a full night out, with an 82 fit score against their portfolio audience.
brief.angle: Frame the app as a platform that sits on top of premium live-event IP and monetizes the whole night, not just the ticket, which suits a long-term holder of sports and media assets. Show that it can reach the 25-29 fans who sit just above the under-25 audience of their portfolio, and that Eldridge could help open doors across its wider holdings.

name_drop.line: Our customers show a 0.767 affinity with A24's audience, the highest in your portfolio, which tells us fans who care about distinctive IP are the ones who want a curated night out.
name_drop.name: A24

name_drop.line: Our customers also overlap strongly with DraftKings at 0.763, so we see the same engaged, event-driven fan that you already know how to serve.
name_drop.name: DraftKings

name_drop.line: Overtime shows a 0.727 affinity with our customers, and we reach the 25-29 fans who are a step older than the under-25 crowd Overtime speaks to.
name_drop.name: Overtime

deck: Lead with the fanbase-specific curation: show how bars, merch and rides are picked for each fanbase, since Eldridge values companies built around premium IP.
Put the audience slide early: your crowd is 25-29 and their portfolio skews under 25, so present yourselves as the next stage of the same fan.
Explain the Ticketmaster, Spotify and Uber comparables as a model: ticketing for the event, personalization for taste, and logistics for the night, combined in one app.
Show how the platform scales across more venues, artists and eventually sports and other live IP, since they look for platforms that can scale.
Include a slide on how Eldridge's wider portfolio could help you, and what a strategic round with a long-term partner would unlock.

openers.line: You hold stakes in the Lakers and the Dodgers, so you know how much of a game day happens outside the game. We do that for concert nights.
openers.name: Los Angeles Lakers

openers.line: A24 is a good example of IP that has a real fanbase behind it. That fan-first idea is what we build our product around.
openers.name: A24

openers.line: A lot of sports media talk, from Bleacher Report to The Bill Simmons Podcast, is about fans caring about the whole experience around the event. That's the space we work in for live music.
openers.name: Bleacher Report

avoid: Do not pitch it as a loose early idea. Eldridge makes strategic, growth and control investments, so bring evidence that the product works.
Do not talk about a quick flip or short-term exit. Their permanent capital is built for long-term partnerships.
Do not lean on the Chelsea sale as a conversation hook. It ended in September 2026, so use their current sports interests instead.
questions: Which fanbases and IP owners do you have real relationships with, and which do you depend on someone else for?
How does this grow beyond concerts into sports and other live events?
Why would a long-term holder invest instead of just partnering, and what would you want from Eldridge's wider portfolio?
